name: funko_pop_pikachu
description: Canonical Pikachu paint: yellow body, black ear tips + eyes, black base disc (component-aware so feet stay yellow), red cheeks + mouth via signed-curvature recess detection. Y-axis is feet→head in the local mesh frame (Funko Pop convention with disc at -Y). Tags map by name via palette_remap; defaults assume palette={yellow:2, black:1, red:4, white:3}.

fingerprint.comment: Funko Pop Pikachu — bilateral, taller than wide, ≥ 2 recesses (eyes + mouth), single body component. Tuned against the canonical 150 mm Funko mesh with disc.

steps.comment: Yellow base coat — full Y range

Base disc — connected component seeded from below the bbox along +Y. The disc is typically a separate sub-mesh on a Funko Pop, so this paints just the disc and leaves the figure's feet yellow. If the disc isn't its own component (older / single-shell Funkos), nothing else nearby gets painted because BFS stops at the body's distinct vertex set.
Eyes — the two largest concave recesses in the upper face area (Y > 0). The signed-curvature detector finds the eye sockets deterministically without pixel guesses.
Mouth — the largest concave recess just below the eyes (Y in [-15, 5]). The mirror flag is OFF because the mouth is a single centered feature.

Cheeks — paired red blush on either side of the mouth. Funko cheeks are subtly raised bulges (convex, not concave), so we use paint_with_mirror + paint_sphere instead of paint_recessed_features. Coordinates are heuristic for a standard 150 mm Funko Pikachu; users with custom-scaled models can pass palette_remap to skip this step.
